prompt: A 58-year-old man with acute myeloid leukemia is being evaluated for hematopoietic cell transplantation. His comorbidities include atrial fibrillation requiring treatment, coronary artery disease with prior myocardial infarction, insulin-treated type 2 diabetes mellitus, a recent transient ischemic attack, depression under psychiatric care, chronic hepatitis with bilirubin at the upper limit of normal, BMI 37 kg/m^2, an infection requiring antimicrobial treatment that will continue after transplant day 0, rheumatoid arthritis, pulmonary diffusion capacity (DLCO) of 70% predicted, and a history of a treated solid tumor. Using the Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Specific Comorbidity Index (HCT-CI), what is his total score, and how should it be interpreted?

rubric_items.text: States the total Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Specific Comorbidity Index (HCT-CI) score for this patient is 15 (exact integer match required).

States the clinical interpretation: High risk (HCT-CI ≥3), with historical original-validation-cohort estimates of approximately 41% 2-year non-relapse mortality and 34% 2-year overall survival (accept equivalent wording).
